title: Making Real Progress In Security From AI

slides.text: Title slide: Making Real Progress In Security From AI, Michael Bargury, Zenity.
Statement slide: We aren't making real progress.
AI security benchmarks from OpenAI and Microsoft shown increasing.
Social post screenshot about AI benchmark progress.
Collage captioned Hackers partying like it's 1999.
Benchmarks go up while hackers party like it's 1999.
Reaction image asking But why?
AI characteristics: weird, gullible, non-deterministic, opaque, and confidently wrong.
Reaction image saying Yes, but beside AI's difficult characteristics.
AI Gold Rush slide.
Gold-rush security problems including costly mistakes, herd mentality, and a lower security bar.
Section slide: Security in a gold rush.
Security in a gold rush with a Good time for that reaction image.
Fixed with AI stamp over gold-rush security problems.
AI guardrails, safety training, and safety classifiers introduced.
Statement: Guardrails are a content moderation technique.
Annotated chat example showing instructions, data, prompt engineering, evasion, and social engineering.
Statement: Injection is the wrong term.
LLMs are generative models doomed to complete and shackled to their context.
Movie still illustrating completion of context.
Prompt injection is not a vulnerability to patch; like malware, it is a problem to manage.
Anthropic report on detecting and countering AI misuse, August 2025.
AI guardrails are soft boundaries and attackers use LLMs too.
Hard boundaries do work; they make an action unreachable.
Case 1 section slide: Supply chain.
AI agent illustration.
AI agent becomes an AI assistant through connected applications.
Screenshot of an AI assistant connected to more than 80 applications.
MCP presented as a universal adapter giving an agent access to third-party tools.
Supply chain is hard; ask npm.
Examples of supply-chain attacks on MCP.
MCP contrasted with npm package locks, version pinning, and integrity checks.
A2A does the exact same thing, with protocol screenshots.
MCP can turn an AI assistant into any agent.
Fixed with AI stamp over the MCP agent-transformation diagram.
Hard boundaries for MCP: pin versions and require approval for new or updated tools.
Case 2 section slide: AI browsers.
Computer Use demo screenshot and warning that it is still risky.
Question: But browser agents are just fine?
Browser-agent product screenshot.
Article screenshot about browser prompt injection and the question: didn't CORS solve this?
AI browsers do not respect robots.txt, CORS, or other web boundaries.
Fixed with AI stamp over the AI-browser boundary problem.
Hard boundary for AI browsers: respect CORS.
Case 3 section slide: Cool designs.
Memory is persistence for attacks, illustrated with a ChatGPT example.
Zero-click attack on ChatGPT illustrated as a persistent compromise chain.
Bio memory tool description showing persistent memory.
Bio memory tool can be abused to compromise future sessions.
Testing memories with sensitive data in the session context.
Testing bio infection by asking directly for memorization.
Testing bio infection: the model refuses to memorize untrusted content.
Testing bio infection: the bio tool appears disabled.
Testing bio infection: untrusted chat data silently disables the bio tool.
Hard boundary: shut down memory when untrusted data enters the context.
Built-in msearch defense prefixes untrusted content with line numbers.
Hard boundary: prefix untrusted context with line numbering to resist line jumps.
Black Hat USA 2024 slide: 15 Ways to Break Your Copilot.
A human must specify the site because AI cannot dynamically choose which site to access.
Hard boundary: do not let AI choose a value that changes environment or tenant scope.
Black Hat USA 2024 slide: Living off Microsoft Copilot.
Copilot requires explicit acceptance before seeing an external message.
Black Hat USA 2025 slide: Invitation Is All You Need.
Hard boundary: external messages must not enter RAG without explicit human approval.
Invitation Is All You Need example of malicious tool chaining.
Hard boundary: tool output cannot invoke another tool.
Black Hat USA 2024 example from 15 Ways to Break Your Copilot.
Statement: Autonomous agents cannot operate on behalf of users.
Question slide: Or can they?
Autonomous agent can run on behalf of the caller ID in an incident record.
Hard boundary: only allow autonomous agents to run for the explicit request invoker.
Transition slide: Let's do an easy one.
Image-rendering attack examples across enterprise AI products.
Image-rendering attacks including ForcedLeak and AgentForce data exfiltration.
Hard boundaries: do not render arbitrary images or rely on allow lists.
Markdown sanitizer examples and linked source repository.
Case 4 section slide.
Question: Does your agent need to write and execute software at runtime?
A ReAct loop is writing and executing software at runtime.
Question: Do we need to regenerate the same automations again and again?
Looking back at how little was known in August 2024.
Summary of hard-boundary lessons for MCP, browsers, memory, tools, rendering, and autonomous agents.
Two categories: AI-is-weird security problems and AI-gold-rush security problems.
IBM 1979 quote: A computer can never be held accountable, so it must never make a management decision.
AI will make business decisions, decisions mean risk, and trustworthy AI is needed.
Thank-you slide with League of Security Experts artwork.
